identityTest.stableIdentity: One Cost Allocation cluster governs reusable rules and immutable executions while preserving separately addressable rule, revision, run and result object identities.
identityTest.versionIdentity: Rule revisions and runs are immutable; corrections append backward supersedes references while every predecessor stays resolvable.

identifierPlanes.modelIdentity: Registry identifier for the cluster; unassigned and never guessed.
identifierPlanes.objectIdentity: Stable identifiers are allocated by the owning aggregate independently of registry model allocation.
identifierPlanes.citationRoot: CostAllocationRun is the citation root; a result is cited as (allocationRunId, resultId).
identifierPlanes.digest: Digests verify content and are never identity.

immutable allocation runs pinned to one rule revision, one axis, one currency and one source period

source-amount derivation, base completeness, tolerances, rounding, discount, reserved-capacity and confidence policy

invariantRules.statement: Every cost assertion declares basis, period and currency.
Quoted price, invoice amount, recognized cost, usage, allocated cost and valuation are separately typed and never substituted.
A model identifier is never substituted for an object identifier, and object-level citation does not depend on registry allocation.
Every allocation run pins exactly one immutable rule revision.
A run has exactly one allocation axis and exactly one currency.
Effective intervals of revisions of one rule are pairwise non-overlapping.
Allocation axis is identity-fixing for a rule; an axis change creates a new rule identity.
Within one run, the sum of target amounts and residual amounts equals sourceAmount within amountTolerance.
Target weights sum to one within weightTolerance over the allocable base; residual share is represented separately.
Every residual carries a closed residualKind and every rounding remainder is materialized.
sourceAmountBasis is declared and ordered sourceAmountDerivation entries sum to sourceAmount.
Allocation base kind, source and completeness are explicit; partial completeness implies a non-zero residual.
Untagged usage remains residual and no implicit default target is permitted.
Parallel axes over intersecting source records are non-additive.
The allocation-run chain is acyclic and a chained run conserves to its cited upstream results, each of which has at most one downstream consumer.
Unused reserved capacity uses exactly one closed treatment: shared-pool-result, separate-chained-run or residual-unused-capacity.
Discount treatment is pinned on the rule revision, allowance identity is retained, and gross and net views are reproducible.
Allocation occurs in source currency; translated results carry rate metadata and never enter conservation or unit-cost calculations.
Allocated cost is never a ledger posting without a separately authorized journal entry.
An allocation result never mutates an invoice or journal master.
Runs and results are immutable; corrections append backward-linked successors with a reason and predecessors remain resolvable.
Confidence remains decomposed into measurement uncertainty, representativeness, commitment-coverage certainty and residual share.
Unit cost pins numerator basis, allocation run, denominator quantity source, metric-definition version, denominator completeness and residual treatment.
Retired rule, run and result identifiers remain resolvable and are never recycled.

holds: Registry namespace and identifier allocation are pending; no identifier has been guessed.
Metric Definition remains the unassigned EM-DAT-05 candidate.
WM-ECO-002 and WM-MAT-008 bindings remain non-assertable until canonical base and relation approval.
Commitment instrument mastership is unbound and no local candidate is introduced.
All referenced bases remain non-canonical reviewable drafts.
The exact Grok review is delivered and reconciled; the single frozen audit is spent and must not be rerun.
